title: Justification for POFMA Correction Direction Issued on 15 February 2024 with Details of Couple's Financial Information
what_it_is: Justification for POFMA Correction Direction Issued on 15 February 2024 with Details of Couple's Financial Information

sections.label: POFMA Correction Direction and CPF disclosure
sections.summary: The POFMA Correction Direction did not identify the couple; disclosing their CPF and MediSave balances was needed to dispel falsehoods in Mr Leong Mun Wai's statement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To be clear, the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act (POFMA) Correction Direction issued on 15 February 2024 did not identify the couple in any way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The disclosure of the couple’s CPF and MediSave balances were necessary to dispel falsehoods in a public statement by Mr Leong Mun Wai about Government assistance to the needy.

sections.label: Public interest data disclosure rules
sections.summary: Agencies must correct the record in the public interest, consistent with the Instruction Manual and Public Sector (Governance) Act data governance standards allowing disclosure if necessary in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Government agencies then have to set the record straight, in the public interest, and this is consistent with the Government's Instruction Manual and the Public Sector (Governance) Act on data governance standards, which provide that, among other reasons, personal data can be disclosed, if necessary, in the public interest.

sections.label: No breach conclusion
sections.summary: The short answer is that there was no breach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The short answer is there was no breach.

sections.label: Questions to Mr Singh and vulnerable families
sections.summary: The questions asked were whether Mr Singh alerted Mr Leong to the couple's situation and why he waited four years, and the first two questions were not answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The questions we asked were: whether Mr Singh did alert Mr Leong to the couple's situation; and second, why Mr Singh waited for four years to do so?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: No disagreement with the process that has been in place all this while and we are definitely not saying that the WP and Mr Singh are going out there on social media platforms to point fingers at the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But I think the original first two questions were not answered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I just want to round back to a point that I made earlier, about not using the vulnerable ones in our community as Trojan horses, as pawns or as chess pieces, because every time I go on night walks, every time I visit the families in the rental flats, the specifics of their situations already pain me.
